newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BEVAN THE UNLIKELY HERO FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN THE UNLIKELY HERO FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Makeshift spinner Michael Bevan proved an unlikely hero on Tuesday as Australia defeated West Indies by 123 runs in the first test.

Bevan claimed three crucial wickets to outshine Shane Warne as Mark Taylor's side relentlessly broke down their opponents' resistance to dismiss West Indies for 296 on the fifth and final day at the Gabba.
The result was a bitter disappointment for West Indies opener Sherwin Campbell, who defied an accurate Australian attack for almost seven hours on his way to a defiant 113.

Bevan, who struggled in both innings in his primary role as a middle order batsman, removed Campbell, number four Carl Hooper (23) and pace bowler Ian Bishop (24) with his left-arm wrist spin at key moments to finish with three for 46 from 14 overs.

"Michael got a lot of work on the ball and turned out to be a useful asset for the side. He's a batsman first and foremost but today he proved just what a very talented cricketer he is," Australia captain Mark Taylor said.
Australia, who beat West Indies' 2-1 in their series in the Caribbean early last year, set a daunting victory target of 420 after opting not to enforce the follow-on on Sunday.
West Indies' hopes of survival diminished dramatically before lunch when Brian Lara was dismissed for 44.
Lara edged a sharp catch to Mark Waugh at second slip after driving rashly at a wide delivery from pace bowler Paul Reiffel.
